reuse.why: Keeps getRangedAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a new getExpectedAmount that re-does the missing/number/range dispatch the existing getScheduledAmount already performs instead of extending that helper.

duplication.why: The inline dispatches at the server sites and the template's own midpoint are removed, yet the null/number/range dispatch now lives in two exported functions (getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount), with getScheduledAmount half-delegating to the other.

placement.why: The rule is in shared/schedules.ts beside getRangedAmount, the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal, and sites only pass value and operator.

scope.why: Focused on the rule, its call sites and the API field, but leaves a step-1 release note whose 'furthest from zero' text the final rule contradicts and adds none for steps 3-4.

maintainability.why: Two near-identical entry points with different signatures (inverse flag vs not) invite future drift and confusion over which to call; the API uses one and the server paths the other.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Server sites (forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, schedule-template.ts) are moved to a new getExpectedAmount rather than the existing getScheduledAmount, which already covered missing, single and ranged amounts.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts restates getScheduledAmount's null check, number branch and getRangedAmount call under a new name and slightly reshaped signature.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and the new parallel getExpectedAmount takes op with an isapprox branch; the five server call sites use the parallel helper instead of getScheduledAmount, while the API mapper and desktop-client sites use getScheduledAmount (the client ones without op).
